newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Bengali activist-novelist wins Magsaysay award. [CORRECTED 08:50 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Bengali activist-novelist wins Magsaysay award. [CORRECTED 08:50 GMT]

text.p: A Bengali novelist who championed the plight of Indian tribal communities was named the winner on Thursday of the 1997 Ramon Magsaysay Award for journalism, literature and creative communication arts.
Mahasweta Devi is cited for "her compassionate crusade through art and activism to claim for tribal peoples a just and honourable place in India's national life", the Magsaysay Foundation said.
"Devi's searing stories and novels not only give voice to India's forgotten tribals but also stress the profound subordination of women in Indian society," the citation read.

Devi started her writing career in 1956 and in 1973 published her watershed novel "Mother of 1084" (correcting title of the book from 1089 to 1084), which depicted a grieving mother coming to terms with her murdered son who joined a violent tribal uprising.
Aside from creative writing, Devi also led a campaign against police, landlords, politicians and officials who abused tribal people.
Devi will receive a certificate and medallion bearing the likeness of Philippine president Ramon Magsaysay who died in a plane crash in 1957. She will also receive a cash prize of $50,000.
Devi is the 36th woman and 35th Indian individual to receive the Ramon Magsaysay Award which was launched in 1958.
